We're working as partners, not as client and contractor. One rule before the task:

Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something
(a source, a number, a quote, a repo, a bug) to make the answer sound more complete or
more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Find real, documented post-mortems of major cloud outages in 2025 (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud or Cloudflare). For each, cite the provider's own incident report and quote what it says the root cause was.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are the real, documented post-mortems I was able to find from the search results, covering major outages at Azure and Cloudflare in 2025. I was unable to find any AWS or Google Cloud post-mortems in the provided results.

---

**Azure Front Door (October 29–30, 2025)**
An 8.5-hour global outage affected Azure Front Door and Azure CDN, taking down portals and Microsoft 365 services.

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | QUOTE: "A specific sequence of customer configuration changes, performed across two different control plane build versions, resulted in incompatible customer configuration metadata being generated." | CLAIM: The root cause was incompatible metadata generated by valid customer configuration changes across different build versions.

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | QUOTE: "These customer configuration changes themselves were valid and non-malicious – however they produced metadata that, when deployed to edge site servers, exposed a latent bug in the data plane." | CLAIM: The crash was triggered by a latent data plane bug that the valid configuration metadata exposed.

**Cloudflare (November 18, 2025)**
A global network outage lasted roughly from 11:20 UTC to 17:06 UTC, initially misdiagnosed as a DDoS attack.

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/cloudflare--2025-11-18--global-network-outage-bot-management/ | QUOTE: "Instead, it was triggered by a change to one of our database systems’ permissions which caused the database to output multiple entries into a “feature file” used by our Bot Management system." | CLAIM: The root cause was a database permission change that caused duplicate entries in the Bot Management feature file.

SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/cloudflare--2025-11-18--global-network-outage-bot-management/ | QUOTE: "The software had a limit on the size of the feature file that was below its doubled size. That caused the software to fail." | CLAIM: The failure mechanism was the feature file doubling in size and exceeding a hard limit in the routing software.

**Cloudflare (December 5, 2025)**
A brief ~25-minute outage caused by 500 HTTP errors across the network.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "Instead, it was triggered by changes being made to our body parsing logic while attempting to detect and mitigate an industry-wide vulnerability disclosed this week in React Server Components." | CLAIM: The root cause was a code change to body parsing logic intended to mitigate a React Server Components vulnerability.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "Unfortunately, in our FL1 version of our proxy, under certain circumstances, the second change of turning off our WAF rule testing tool caused an error state that resulted in 500 HTTP error codes to be served from our network." | CLAIM: The specific trigger was turning off the WAF rule testing tool, which caused an error state in the FL1 proxy.

**Cloudflare (September 12, 2025)**
A dashboard and API outage triggered by a bug in the Tenant Service API calls.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage/ | QUOTE: "This bug caused repeated, unnecessary calls to the Tenant Service API. The API calls were managed by a React useEffect hook, but we mistakenly included a problematic object in its dependency array." | CLAIM: The root cause was a frontend bug where a React useEffect dependency array caused infinite API calls.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage/ | QUOTE: "Because this object was recreated on every state or prop change, React treated it as 'always new,' causing the useEffect to re-run each time." | CLAIM: The mechanism was React interpreting the recreated object as new, triggering continuous re-runs of the API call.

**Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 (July 14, 2025)**
A 62-minute global outage of Cloudflare's public DNS resolver.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-1-1-1-1-incident-on-july-14-2025/ | QUOTE: "The outage occurred because of a misconfiguration of legacy systems used to maintain the infrastructure that advertises Cloudflare’s IP addresses to the Internet." | CLAIM: The root cause was a misconfiguration in legacy systems advertising IP addresses.

SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-1-1-1-1-incident-on-july-14-2025/ | QUOTE: "the prefixes associated with the 1.1.1.1 Resolver service were inadvertently included alongside the prefixes that were intended for the new DLS service." | CLAIM: The specific error was the inclusion of 1.1.1.1 prefixes in a configuration meant for a new DLS service.

---

**Missing items:**

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: AWS post-mortems for major cloud outages in 2025. The search results did not contain any AWS incident reports or root cause analyses.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Google Cloud post-mortems for major cloud outages in 2025. The search results did not contain any Google Cloud incident reports or root cause analyses.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Direct links to the primary Microsoft Azure or Cloudflare blog domains for the Azure Front Door incident. The Azure Front Door post-mortem was sourced via postmortem.io rather than a direct Microsoft Azure blog URL. (The Cloudflare incidents were sourced directly from blog.cloudflare.com.)
